title: The Displacement Bench
summary: Charge a capacitor and find its displacement current and the magnetic field it makes between the plates.
subject: physics
learningOutcome: The student can find the capacitance and charging rate of a plate capacitor, the displacement current from a changing field, and the magnetic field it produces between the plates.

levels.title: Charging a capacitor
levels.adds: Baseline: C = ε₀A/d and I = C dV/dt (Ex 8.1).
hints: The plate area is π times the radius squared, in m².

levels.title: Displacement current
levels.adds: New idea: a changing electric flux is a current, I_d = ε₀ dflux/dt, which keeps the current continuous (Section 8.2).
hints: I_d = ε₀ A dE/dt, with A in m².
Between the plates the displacement current equals the conduction current in the wires.
So the total current has no break at the plates.

levels.title: An AC capacitor
levels.adds: More steps: find the rms current, then the field made by the peak displacement current (Ex 8.2).
hints: The peak current is √2 times the rms current.
Inside the plates B = μ₀ r I_d/(2πR²).

misconceptions: No current flows between the plates, so Kirchhoff’s rule fails there
A magnetic field needs a moving charge, never a changing electric field
The conduction and displacement currents differ in an AC capacitor
